newsitem.title: USA: NYS LIPA seeks FERC clearance of LILCO plan.
newsitem.headline: NYS LIPA seeks FERC clearance of LILCO plan.

text.p: The Long Island Power Authority said an application is being filed Thursday with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission seeking approval of its acquisition of Long Island Lighting Co's transmission and distribution system.

The authority said the FERC application explains how the transaction between LIPA and LILCO, which is merging with Brooklyn Union Gas Co, would lower both wholesale and retail electric rates on Long Island.

The LIPA statement also said the $4.5 billion interest rate swap reported Tuesday by Bear Stearns will "help assure electric customers that they will receive the average 17 percent rate reductions even if interest rates increase between now and the time LIPA issues bonds to assume or refinance certain LILCO debt and preferred."
It said the hedge was purchased by LILCO and Brooklyn Union on behalf of LIPA, which will reimburse the companies for the cost of the hedge, plus carrying costs, when the LIPA transaction is closed.

Last week, LIPA said, it and the two utilities submitted ruling requests to the U.S. Internal Revenue Service to confirm that LIPA's purchase of LILCO stock will not be subject to a corproate tax under current fecderal law, the bonds to be issued by LIPA to acquire the stock will be exempt from federal income tax, and the income received by LIPA after it begins to operate as a public utility will not be subject to federal income tax.
